title: feature-map
description: What a repository declares about its own features and the code paths that implement them. Read by the coverage gate, which refuses a pull request touching a governed file that no feature claims.

product.description: The product this map describes. Free text, and the only field here purely for a human reading the file.

governedRoots.description:
The roots the gate governs. A changed file outside every one of these is ignored; a changed file inside one MUST be claimed by some feature's codePaths or the gate fails.

Required, and required for a reason. hopperguard kept these in its workflow as a JavaScript constant, which meant the one setting that decides what the gate even looks at was invisible to the map, unreadable by a shared action, and different per repository with nothing comparing them. A gate whose scope lives in its own implementation cannot be extracted.

An EMPTY array is legal and means the gate governs nothing. That is a real state a repository may want while adopting the map, and it is deliberately distinguishable from the field being absent -- which is now impossible, because it is required. An absent key that reads as an empty list is exactly the failure this schema exists to make unrepresentable.

featureGroups.description: The groups. Order is presentation only and carries no meaning.

groupKey.description:
A group's stable identifier. SCREAMING_SNAKE, which is not a preference -- it is what all three live maps already use, measured: every group key in hopperguard, rozcards and card-sorter matches this today. A schema that invented a different convention would invalidate the entire corpus on its first run and call that a finding.

It appears in gate output, in URLs and in generated diagram filenames, so it must survive all three without escaping.

featureKey.description:
A feature's stable identifier: its group's key, a dot, then one segment -- `HOPS.CREATE`.

Also measured rather than imposed. All 133 feature keys in hopperguard are exactly `<groupKey>.<segment>` with a single dot, and none has two. The dotted form is what makes a feature key globally unique by construction rather than by luck.

The schema can only enforce the SHAPE here, because JSON Schema cannot compare a value against its parent's. That the prefix matches the group it is nested in is checked in code, where it catches a feature pasted into the wrong group -- an error that is otherwise completely silent.

pathGlob.description:
A repository-relative path or glob, using FORWARD SLASHES only.

The `not` below refuses three things: an absolute path, a Windows drive letter, and any `..` segment.

Backslashes are refused outright rather than normalised, and that is the load-bearing decision. An earlier version of this pattern enumerated the forward-slash forms of traversal and was bypassed three ways in one review: `..\\..\\etc`, `\\absolute\\path` and `src\\..\\..\\x` were all accepted, because every clause it had checked for `/`. Banning the character removes the whole class instead of the instances -- and costs nothing, since git reports paths with forward slashes on every platform, so a backslash here is already wrong before it is dangerous.

The bare string `..` is refused too. It was accepted by the earlier pattern, which required a leading or trailing slash and so matched `../x` and `x/../y` while missing the shortest escape of all.

featureGroup.description:
A group of features, or -- where a repository does not need the inner level -- a feature in its own right.

## Why this is a union rather than one fixed depth

Measured across the three live maps in this fleet: hopperguard nests 133 features under 28 groups, while rozcards' 11 groups and card-sorter's 4 carry their code paths directly. Neither is wrong. hopperguard's feature granularity is real and is what its gate reports against, so flattening would DESTROY information; and requiring two levels everywhere would make the other two wrap every group in a synthetic single feature nobody asked for, to satisfy a reader rather than to describe anything.

So a group carries `codePaths` OR `features`, never both and never neither. That is asserted here rather than left to the gate, because a group with both has no defined meaning and a group with neither silently governs nothing -- and a feature that claims no paths is indistinguishable, to the gate, from a feature that does not exist. Across all three live maps today, zero groups violate this.

feature.description: One feature, and the code that implements it.

relatedComponents.description: Components this feature reads or renders but does not own. Documentation for a human; the gate does not use it, and a path here does NOT claim a file.

codePaths.description: The files this feature owns. `minItems: 1` is the point of the field: an empty list claims nothing, so a feature carrying one is invisible to the gate while looking, in the file, exactly like a feature that is covered.
